name: Manticore
description: A man-eating creature of Persian origin, first described in Greek by the physician-historian Ctesias in the 5th century BCE. The manticore has the body of a lion, the face of a man with three rows of teeth, and a tail tipped with venomous spines or a scorpion's sting.

aliases.name: Martichora
aliases.meaning: transliteration of the Old Persian name

origin: Originally placed in 'India' by Ctesias and his Greek and Latin successors. In medieval bestiaries and heraldry the creature is generic to far-eastern and exotic landscapes.
